label: The Kontsevich Integrals
notes: Open the lecture. The Kontsevich integral is the universal Vassiliev invariant, an analytic formula taking values in the algebra of chord diagrams. The lecture explains its definition by iterated integrals along a Morse-positioned knot, its invariance, and why it dominates all finite type invariants.

label: Knots in Slices
notes: Place the knot in space so the height function is Morse, with finitely many critical points. At each height the knot meets a horizontal plane in finitely many points, giving a configuration that evolves continuously with height. Pairs of strands at each level are the data integrated to build the invariant.

label: The Iterated Integral
notes: Define the integral as a sum over the number of chords, integrating over increasing heights where chosen pairs of strands are joined. Each term carries a chord diagram recording which strands are paired and a sign from local orientation. The result is a formal series valued in the algebra of chord diagrams.

label: Invariance and Correction
notes: Show the raw integral is invariant under deformations that keep the Morse structure but changes at critical points where strands turn around. Dividing by the integral of a standard unknotted hump corrects this, yielding a genuine isotopy invariant. Convergence and the four-term relation make every step well defined.

label: Universality
notes: State the central theorem: the Kontsevich integral is the universal Vassiliev invariant, meaning every finite type invariant is obtained by composing it with some weight system. Combined with the realization theorem, this proves that weight systems and Vassiliev invariants coincide, closing the loop opened in the previous lectures.

label: Recap
notes: Close the lecture. The Kontsevich integral assigns to a knot a series of chord diagrams through iterated integrals over a Morse height function, corrected by the standard hump. It is the universal finite type invariant, dominating all others. The final lecture surveys further important topics in knot theory.
